outcome: Impact of pain on daily living
cohort: 49 English or Spanish speaking patients with publicly funded prenatal care who underwent a cesarean birth at a single large tertiary care center
finding: Qualitative analysis revealed two overarching domains of patient experience: the experience of pain after cesarean birth (meaningful experience, pain not aligned with expectations, limitations caused by pain) and pain management and opioid use after cesarean birth (desire for nonpharmacologic pain management, positive and negative experiences using opioids, and hesitancy and perceived judgment regarding opioid use).
